The solar Fe/H and Mg/H are given, but the absolute solar Si abundance is not needed.  

For Star 1  

\[
[\text{Fe/H}]_1 =0 \;\Rightarrow\; \frac{\text{Fe}_1}{\text{H}} = \frac{\text{Fe}_\odot}{\text{H}} .
\]

\[
[\text{Si/Fe}]_1 =0.3\;\text{dex}\;\Rightarrow\; 
\frac{\text{Si}_1}{\text{Fe}_1}= \frac{\text{Si}_\odot}{\text{Fe}_\odot}\times10^{0.3}.
\]

Thus  

\[
\frac{\text{Si}_1}{\text{H}} = \frac{\text{Si}_\odot}{\text{H}}\times10^{0.3}.
\]

For Star 2  

\[
[\text{Mg/H}]_2 =0 \;\Rightarrow\; \frac{\text{Mg}_2}{\text{H}} = \frac{\text{Mg}_\odot}{\text{H}} .
\]

\[
[\text{Mg/Si}]_2 =0.3\;\text{dex}\;\Rightarrow\;
\frac{\text{Mg}_2}{\text{Si}_2}= \frac{\text{Mg}_\odot}{\text{Si}_\odot}\times10^{0.3}.
\]

Since \(\frac{\text{Mg}_2}{\text{H}} = \frac{\text{Mg}_\odot}{\text{H}}\),

\[
\frac{1}{\text{Si}_2/\text{H}} = \frac{1}{\text{Si}_\odot/\text{H}}\times10^{0.3}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\frac{\text{Si}_2}{\text{H}} = \frac{\text{Si}_\odot}{\text{H}}\times10^{-0.3}.
\]

Therefore  

\[
\frac{\text{Si}_1}{\text{Si}_2}= \frac{10^{0.3}}{10^{-0.3}} = 10^{0.6}\approx 3.98.
\]

The ratio of silicon atoms in Star 1 to Star 2 is about 4, matching option **D**.

**Answer: D**
